from.place: the coefficient-twist construction and its scalar-extension normalization, as used by the route lemma lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change

title: There is exactly one normalized semilinear family on the signed Tate lines.
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a field $L$ equipped with an algebra structure over $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and finite-dimensional over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, an algebra map $\iota:E\to_{\mathbf Q_\ell}L$, and a scheme $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. For $H=E,L$ let $R_H=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{H,S}$ be the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], let $j:\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_L$ be the restriction of $\iota$ and $c:R_E\to R_L$ the completed coefficient map induced by $\iota$ [def-weil-completed-integral-scalar-data]. Let $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S$ be the root-limit sheaf and $\mathcal O_H(1)_S$ its discrete integral coefficient tensor with its completed $R_H$-action and pure tensors $b\otimes x$ ($b$ a local section of the constant sheaf $(\mathcal O_H)_S$, $x$ a local section of $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S$) [def-pur-twist-sheaves], and let $\mathcal O_H(m)$, $m\in\mathbf Z$, be its signed powers of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]: $R_H$ for $m=0$, tensor powers over $R_H$ for $m>0$, and the sheaf Hom $\mathcal Hom_{R_H}(\mathcal O_H(-m),R_H)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] for $m<0$, with its evaluation. Let $\operatorname{TwistScalarMaps}(\ell,E,S,L,\iota)$ be the set of families $c=(c_m)_{m\in\mathbf Z}$ of morphisms of $R_E$-module sheaves $c_m:\mathcal O_E(m)\to\operatorname{Res}_c\mathcal O_L(m)$, where $\operatorname{Res}_c$ is restriction of scalars along $c$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For such a family impose the following normalization equations, on sections over every object $U$ of the small pro-etale site: (i) $c_0=c$; (ii) $c_1(b\otimes x)=j(b)\otimes x$ for every local section $b$ of $(\mathcal O_E)_S$ and $x$ of $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S$; (iii) for every $m\geq1$, $c_{m+1}(x\otimes y)=c_m(x)\otimes c_1(y)$ for sections $x$ in degree $m$ and $y$ in degree $1$; and (iv) for every $n\geq0$, every section $f$ in degree $-(n+1)$ and every section $x$ in degree $n+1$ over $U$, the evaluation of $c_{-(n+1)}(f)$ (at the identity of $U$) on $c_{n+1}(x)$ equals $c(f(x))$. Then there exists exactly one family $c\in\operatorname{TwistScalarMaps}(\ell,E,S,L,\iota)$ satisfying (i)-(iv).

proof.text: Degrees $0$ and $1$. Put $c_0=c$, which is $R_E$-linear into $\operatorname{Res}_cR_L$ by definition of restriction of scalars. In degree $1$, $\mathcal O_H(1)_S=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S}(\mathcal O_H)_S$; since the constant map $(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S\to(\mathcal O_E)_S\to(\mathcal O_L)_S$ induced by $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{j}\mathcal O_L$ is the structure map of $(\mathcal O_L)_S$, functoriality of the sheafified tensor in its second factor gives an additive sheaf map $c_1=\mathrm{id}\otimes(j)_S$ with $c_1(b\otimes x)=j(b)\otimes x$, so (ii) holds by construction. Semilinearity: by clause 3 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] and the isomorphism $\beta_{H,S}:\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,S}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S}(\mathcal O_H)_S\xrightarrow{\sim}R_H$ of [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-tensor-normalization], local sections $r=\beta_{E}(\rho\otimes b')$ generate $R_E$ additively and act by $r(x\otimes b)=\rho x\otimes b'b$. Applying that node to the finite extension $\iota(E)\subset L$, its map $i_{EL}$ equals $c$ (both are the unique map to the limit $R_L$ with the same finite projections, [def-weil-completed-integral-scalar-data]), and $i_{EL}\beta_E=\beta_L(1\otimes q_{EL})$ gives $c(r)=\beta_L(\rho\otimes j(b'))$. Hence $c_1(r\,v)=\rho x\otimes j(b')j(b)=c(r)\,c_1(v)$ for $v=x\otimes b$; by additivity and local generation $c_1$ is $R_E$-linear into $\operatorname{Res}_c\mathcal O_L(1)_S$.

source.place: root-limit tensor $\mathcal O_E(1)_S=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S\otimes\mathcal O_E$ and coefficient maps

proof.text: Linearization. Let $b:\mathcal O_E(1)_S\otimes_{R_E}R_L\to\mathcal O_L(1)_S$ be the $R_L$-linear map $v\otimes s\mapsto s\,c_1(v)$ (well defined on the balanced sheaf tensor by Step 1). By clause 2 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] there is a pro-etale covering $\{V_k\to S\}$ and generators $\zeta_k$ with $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S|_{V_k}=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,V_k}\zeta_k$; by clause 3 $\mathcal O_H(1)_S|_{V_k}$ is free of rank one over $R_H$ on $1\otimes\zeta_k$. Since $c_1(1\otimes\zeta_k)=1\otimes\zeta_k$, on $V_k$ the map $b$ is, in these bases, the unit isomorphism $u_c:R_E\otimes_{R_E}R_L\simeq R_L$, $r\otimes s\mapsto s\,c(r)$, of [def-sp-canonical-scalar-extension-maps]. A sheaf map that is an isomorphism on each member of a covering is an isomorphism [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism], so $b$ is an isomorphism; both lines are locally isomorphic to $R_E$, resp. $R_L$, on a covering of the final object $S$.

Positive degrees. Apply [lem-pur-signed-line-scalar-tensor-tower] (the pro-etale site of $S$ has finite limits and final object $S$) to $R_0=R_E\xrightarrow{c}R_1=R_L\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}R_2=R_L$, $L_0=\mathcal O_E(1)_S$, $L_1=L_2=\mathcal O_L(1)_S$, $b_{01}=b$ of Step 2, $b_{12}$ the multiplication comparison $L_1\otimes_{R_L}R_L\simeq L_1$ and $b_{02}=b_{12}(b_{01}\otimes1)$; the lines are locally free of rank one by Step 2. Its signed powers $L_i^{[m]}$ are the $\mathcal O_H(m)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] (same tensor powers and sheaf duals). Define $c_m(x)=b_{01,m}(x\otimes1)$ for $m\geq0$; it is $R_E$-linear into $\operatorname{Res}_c$, as $b_{01,m}$ is $R_L$-linear and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ is $c$-semilinear. The unit comparison $b_{01,0}$ gives $c_0(r)=c(r)$, which is (i), and $b_{01,1}=b$ gives back $c_1$ of Step 1. For $a=m\geq1$, $b=1$ the tower's multiplicativity $b_{01,m+1}(\mu^{m,1}\otimes1)=\mu^{m,1}(b_{01,m}\otimes b_{01,1})\sigma$, with $\mu^{m,1}$ the defining identification $L^{\otimes m}\otimes L=L^{\otimes(m+1)}$ and $\sigma((x\otimes y)\otimes1)=(x\otimes1)\otimes(y\otimes1)$, gives $c_{m+1}(x\otimes y)=c_m(x)\otimes c_1(y)$, which is (iii).

source.place: definition of positive signed powers $\Lambda(1)^{\otimes m}$

proof.text: Negative degrees. For $n\geq0$ put $c_{-(n+1)}(f)=b_{01,-(n+1)}(f\otimes1)$, where by [lem-pur-signed-line-scalar-tensor-tower] $b_{01,-(n+1)}=\beta_{01,n+1}\circ(-)\circ b_{01,n+1}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism ($\beta_{01,n+1}$ is the isomorphism of that node, $b_{01,n+1}$ that of Step 3). It is $c$-semilinear as in Step 3. The tower's evaluation identity $\operatorname{ev}(b_{01,-(n+1)}(f\otimes s),b_{01,n+1}(x\otimes t))=c(f(x))st$ with $s=t=1$ is $\operatorname{ev}(c_{-(n+1)}(f),c_{n+1}(x))=c(f(x))$; evaluated at the identity of $U$ this is (iv).

source.place: definition of negative signed powers by sheaf Hom

proof.text: Existence. Steps 1, 3 and 4 define every $c_m$ as a morphism of sheaves of $R_E$-modules $\mathcal O_E(m)\to\operatorname{Res}_c\mathcal O_L(m)$, so $c\in\operatorname{TwistScalarMaps}(\ell,E,S,L,\iota)$; (ii) holds by Step 1, (i) and (iii) by Step 3, (iv) by Step 4. No gluing is needed: all maps are global sheaf maps.

Uniqueness. Let $c,c'$ both satisfy (i)-(iv). Then $c_0=c'_0$ by (i). The sheafified tensor $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S\otimes(\mathcal O_E)_S$ is locally generated additively by pure tensors $b\otimes x$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], on which $c_1,c'_1$ agree by (ii); additive sheaf maps agreeing on local generators are equal, so $c_1=c'_1$. Inductively, if $c_m=c'_m$ ($m\geq1$), then $c_{m+1},c'_{m+1}$ agree on the local generators $x\otimes y$ of $\mathcal O_E(m)\otimes_{R_E}\mathcal O_E(1)$ by (iii), hence are equal. For degree $-(n+1)$ and a section $f$ over $U$: the $R_L$-linear maps $\varphi=c_{-(n+1)}(f)$ and $\varphi'=c'_{-(n+1)}(f)$ on $\mathcal O_L(n+1)|_U$ satisfy, by (iv) applied at every $V\to U$ to $f|_V$ and the naturality of $c,c'$ and of evaluation under restriction, $\varphi(c_{n+1}(x))=\varphi'(c_{n+1}(x))$ for all sections $x$ over all $V\to U$. As $b_{01,n+1}$ is an isomorphism (Step 3), the sections $s\,c_{n+1}(x)$ generate $\mathcal O_L(n+1)$ locally, so $\varphi=\varphi'$ by $R_L$-linearity. Hence $c=c'$.
